63552-armazindy-the-poems-and-prose-sket.creator: Unknown
63552-armazindy-the-poems-and-prose-sket.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Armazindy;—fambily name _Ballenger_,—you’ll find the same, As her Daddy answered it, In the old War-rickords yit,— And, like him, she’s airnt the good Will o’ all the neighborhood.— Name ain’t down in _History_,— But, i jucks! Folks is got respec’ fer _her_— Armazindy Ballenger!

arxiv-2012-01369.title: Improving Solution Quality of Bounded Max-Sum Algorithm to Solve DCOPs involving Hard and Soft Constraints
arxiv-2012-01369.creator: Md. Musfiqur Rahman, Mashrur Rashik, Md. Mamun-or-Rashid, Md. Mosaddek Khan
arxiv-2012-01369.description: Abstract Bounded Max-Sum (BMS) is a message-passing algorithm that provides approximation solution to a specific form of decentralized coordination problems, namely Distributed Constrained Optimization Problems (DCOPs). In particular, BMS algorithm is able to solve problems of this type having large search space at the expense of low computational cost.

arxiv-2103-13736.title: Deep Similarity Learning for Sports Team Ranking PubID: pubid: 978-0-7381-1236-7/21/$31.00 ©2021 IEEE
arxiv-2103-13736.creator: Daniel Yazbek, Jonathan Sandile Sibindi, Terence L. Van Zyl †
arxiv-2103-13736.description: Abstract Sports data is more readily available and consequently, there has been an increase in the amount of sports analysis, predictions and rankings in the literature. Sports are unique in their respective stochastic nature, making analysis, and accurate predictions valuable to those involved in the sport.

arxiv-2108-11405.title: The Earth term in pulsar timing residuals is out of phase among the pulsars Journal: a NANOGrav Memorandum
arxiv-2108-11405.creator: Hyo Sun Park, Andrea Lommen
arxiv-2108-11405.description: Abstract We aim to resolve a misunderstanding about whether the so-called “Earth term” in the pulsar timing response to a gravitational wave is in phase among a set of pulsars. We note that the misunderstanding has potentially arisen from the statements that the Earth term is “coherent” or “builds up coherently” among the pulsars.

arxiv-2206-13561.title: A Search for Unbound Stellar Companions to Pulsar J1124 − - 5916
arxiv-2206-13561.creator: C. S. Kochanek
arxiv-2206-13561.description: Abstract We searched for and found no higher mass ( > ⁣ ∼ 3 ​ M ⊙ \mathrel{\raise 1.29167pt\hbox{$>$}\mkern-14.0mu\lower 2.58334pt\hbox{$\sim$}}3M_{\odot} ) unbound binary stellar companions to the progenitor of pulsar J1124 − - 5916. There are lower mass candidates, but they all have high probabilities of being false positives.

arxiv-2301-10571.title: Leveraging Planning Landmarks for Hybrid Online Goal Recognition
arxiv-2301-10571.creator: Nils Wilken, Lea Cohausz, Johannes Schaum, Stefan Lüdtke, Christian Bartelt, Heiner Stuckenschmidt
arxiv-2301-10571.description: Abstract Goal recognition is an important problem in many application domains (e.g., pervasive computing, intrusion detection, computer games, etc.). In many application scenarios it is important that goal recognition algorithms can recognize goals of an observed agent as fast as possible and with minimal domain knowledge.

arxiv-2305-10845.title: Tapir : Learning Adaptive Revision for Incremental Natural Language Understanding with a Two-Pass Model
arxiv-2305-10845.creator: Patrick Kahardipraja Brielen Madureira David Schlangen
arxiv-2305-10845.description: Abstract Language is by its very nature incremental in how it is produced and processed. This property can be exploited by NLP systems to produce fast responses, which has been shown to be beneficial for real-time interactive applications. Recent neural network-based approaches for incremental processing mainly use RNNs or Transformers.

arxiv-2308-07893.title: Memory-and-Anticipation Transformer for Online Action Understanding
arxiv-2308-07893.creator: Jiahao Wang, Guo Chen, Yifei Huang, Limin Wang, Tong Lu
arxiv-2308-07893.description: Abstract Most existing forecasting systems are memory-based methods, which attempt to mimic human forecasting ability by employing various memory mechanisms and have progressed in temporal modeling for memory dependency. Nevertheless, an obvious weakness of this paradigm is that it can only model limited historical dependence and can not transcend the past.

arxiv-2310-08428.title: S ​ G SG -classes, Singular Symplectic Geometry and Order-Preserving Isomorphisms
arxiv-2310-08428.creator: Alessandro Pietro Contini
arxiv-2310-08428.description: Abstract Abstract The geometric theory of pseudo-differential and Fourier Integral Operators relies on the symplectic structure of cotangent bundles. If one is to study calculi with some specific feature adapted to a geometric situation, the corresponding notion of cotangent bundle needs to be adapted as well and leads to spaces with a singular symplectic structure.

arxiv-2311-14842.title: A Characterization of Optimal-Rate Linear Homomorphic Secret Sharing Schemes, and Applications
arxiv-2311-14842.creator: Keller Blackwell, Mary Wootters
arxiv-2311-14842.description: Abstract A Homomorphic Secret Sharing (HSS) scheme is a secret-sharing scheme that shares a secret x x among s s servers, and additionally allows an output client to reconstruct some function f ⁡ ( x ) f(x) , using information that can be locally computed by each server.

arxiv-2401-05237.title: 3D model for surface accumulation of chiral and non-chiral microswimmers
arxiv-2401-05237.creator: Danne M. van Roon, Giorgio Volpe, Margarida M. Telo da Gama, Nuno A. M. Araújo
arxiv-2401-05237.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Danne M. van Roon, Giorgio Volpe, Margarida M. Telo da Gama, Nuno A. M. Araújo. Persistent motion of microswimmers near boundaries is known to result in surface accumulation. Recently it was shown experimentally that surface accumulation of microswimmers is impacted primarily by steric forces and short-ranged hydrodynamics. A way to control surface accumulation is by reducing the contact surface area between swimmers and surface by modifying its topography, typically through the application of microscale structure.

arxiv-2503-07276.title: A Systematic Review of ECG Arrhythmia Classification: Adherence to Standards, Fair Evaluation, and Embedded Feasibility
arxiv-2503-07276.creator: Guilherme A. L. Silva, Pedro H. L. Silva, Gladston J. P. Moreira, Vander L. S. Freitas
arxiv-2503-07276.description: Abstract The classification of electrocardiogram (ECG) signals is crucial for early detection of arrhythmias and other cardiac conditions. However, despite advances in machine learning-based approaches, a significant portion of the literature does not adhere to key standardization protocols, leading to inconsistencies in performance evaluation and real-world applicability.

pmc-10738332.title: CHARACTERIZING NURSING HOME VISITATION POLICIES AND PROCESSES DURING THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC
pmc-10738332.creator: Courtney Hawes, Joan Brazier, Amy Meehan, Emily Gabois
pmc-10738332.description: The COVID-19 pandemic drastically changed how nursing homes facilitated visitation between residents and their families. Nursing homes needed to modify visitation approaches in response to changing policies and guidelines from varying governing bodies. Additionally, restrictions were constantly adjusted due to fluctuations in COVID-19 infection rates within facilities and the larger communities in which they exist.

pmc-11415845.title: The methodology of health education programs in schools—Qualitative study
pmc-11415845.creator: Roberta Marković, Aleksandra Ignjatović, Aleksandar Višnjić, Miodrag Stojanović, Marija Andjelković Apostolović, Suzana Otasević
pmc-11415845.description: ObjectiveTo assess strengths and weaknesses of the methodology of health education programs, carried out in the period 2010–2020, in schools in Serbia.DesignQualitative study, a thematic analysis approach.SiteRepresentatives of Public Health institutions, Serbian biggest nongovernmental organization, Youth organization, Ministry of education and municipality.ParticipantsNine professionals working in the field of Public Health and Health education.

pmc-11425859.title: Biochemical Properties of CARM1: Impact on Western Blotting and Proteomic Studies
pmc-11425859.creator: Julie Bourassa, Genevieve Paris, Laura Trinkle-Mulcahy, Jocelyn Côté
pmc-11425859.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). CARM1 is an arginine methyltransferase that has crucial roles in a number of cellular pathways and is being explored as a therapeutic target in diseases such as cancer and neurodegenerative disorders. Its deregulation at the protein level was found to have potential prognostic value, and as such, its protein levels are regularly assessed through the common practice of western blotting (WB). Our group uncovered that CARM1 has biochemical properties that complicate its analysis by standard WB sample preparation techniques.

pmc-11536687.title: Presynaptic Proteins and Their Roles in Visual Processing by the Retina
pmc-11536687.creator: Wallace B. Thoreson, David Zenisek
pmc-11536687.description: The sense of vision begins in the retina, where light is detected and processed through a complex series of synaptic connections into meaningful information relayed to the brain via retinal ganglion cells. Light responses begin as tonic and graded signals in photoreceptors, later emerging from the retina as a series of spikes from ganglion cells.

pmc-11727218.title: Opening the AI Black Box: Distilling Machine-Learned Algorithms into Code
pmc-11727218.creator: Eric J. Michaud, Isaac Liao, Vedang Lad, Ziming Liu, Anish Mudide, Chloe Loughridge, Zifan Carl Guo, Tara Rezaei Kheirkhah, Mateja Vukelić, Max Tegmark
pmc-11727218.description: Can we turn AI black boxes into code? Although this mission sounds extremely challenging, we show that it is not entirely impossible by presenting a proof-of-concept method, MIPS, that can synthesize programs based on the automated mechanistic interpretability of neural networks trained to perform the desired task, auto-distilling the learned algorithm into Python code.

pmc-12645368.title: Strong Changes in Soil Nutrient Stocks in Northern Forests Over Four Decades
pmc-12645368.creator: Marie Spohn, Erik Karltun, Johan Stendahl
pmc-12645368.description: Northern forests are currently taking up large quantities of carbon due to tree growth. Yet, it is not known how the stocks of soil nutrients have responded to this increase in biomass. Therefore, we analyzed thousands of forest soils in Sweden over the last four decades.

pmc-12656092.title: Adaptive Label Refinement Network for Domain Generalization in Compound Fault Diagnosis
pmc-12656092.creator: Qiyan Du, Jiajia Yao, Jingyuan Yang, Fengmiao Tu, Suixian Yang
pmc-12656092.description: Highlights What are the main findings? A novel label refinement framework is proposed for compound fault diagnosis under source-scarce conditions, which iteratively evolves soft labels to enhance domain generalization.A KL-divergence-based stability coefficient autonomously guides the iterative label refinement process. What is the implication of the main finding?

pmc-12733843.title: Decoding Bromodomain and Extra-Terminal Domain Protein-Mediated Epigenetic Mechanisms in Human Uterine Fibroids
pmc-12733843.creator: Qiwei Yang, Somayeh Vafaei, Ali Falahati, Azad Khosh, Mervat M. Omran, Tao Bai, Maria Victoria Bariani, Mohamed Ali, Thomas G. Boyer, Ayman Al-Hendy
pmc-12733843.description: Uterine Fibroids (UFs) are the most common benign tumors in women of reproductive age, affecting ~77% of women overall and are clinically manifest in ~25% by age 50. Bromodomain and extra-terminal domain (BET) proteins play key roles in epigenetic transcriptional regulation, influencing many biological processes, such as proliferation, differentiation, and DNA damage response.

pmc-12768803.title: PP15 The Appropriateness Of Translation Of Patient-Reported Outcome Measures In Swahili-Speaking Regions Of Sub-Saharan Africa – A Case Study
pmc-12768803.creator: Magdalena Moshi, Theresia Ambroce Ottaru, Rosemarie Mwaipopo
pmc-12768803.description: IntroductionPatient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) are used to quantify health-related quality of life and generate utility data for economic evaluations. Accurate translation and adaptation of PROMs into non-European languages, such as Swahili, is essential for ensuring the intended health information is captured. A case study evaluated the appropriateness of current Swahili PROMs translations and determined whether these captured a person’s health.

pmc-13040333.title: Effects of fullerenol C60 on the liver, heart and brain tissues of streptozotocin-induced diabetic rats with sepsis
pmc-13040333.creator: Necmiye Şengel, Ömer Kubat, Laman Farajsoylu, Ahmet Çağri Büyükkasap, Muharrem Atli, Şaban Cem Sezen, Hasan Bostanci, Kürşat Dikmen, Işin Güneş, Fatma Er, Mustafa Kavutçu, Mustafa Arslan
pmc-13040333.description: In the present study, the protective effects of fullerenol C60, a nanomaterial with antioxidant properties, were investigated against sepsis-induced multiple organ failure in liver, heart and brain tissues using a sepsis model [cecal ligation and puncture (CLP)] in diabetic rats.

pmc-13632907.title: Voice-Enabled Virtual Patients for Interactive Training in Standardized Clinical Assessment: Mixed Methods Pilot Study
pmc-13632907.creator: Veronica Bossio Botero, Vijay Yadav, Jacob Ouyang, Anzar Abbas, Michelle Worthington
pmc-13632907.description: BackgroundTraining mental health clinicians to conduct standardized clinical assessments is challenging due to a lack of scalable, realistic practice opportunities. Traditional methods often fail to prepare trainees for the variability and complexity of real-world patient interactions, potentially impacting data quality in clinical trials.
